title: Polyglot API adapter for schema evolution: translate legacy v1/v2 requests to v3 streaming and tool-call surfaces
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in runtime adapter that accepts legacy schema versions and translates requests/responses to the current v3 contract; enabled via X-Redwood-Enable-Polyglot header or feature flag. No breaking behavior by default. Doc notes on deprecation timeline included.
description: Motivation: customers running older OpenAI-compatible clients (schema v1/v2) hit multiple failure modes when we rolled v3 structured output and expanded tool-calling semantics. This PR introduces a runtime "polyglot" adapter that negotiates schema version via headers and request shape, translates legacy request/response envelopes into the v3 shapes used by the serving runtime, and provides graceful degradation and observability hooks. The adapter is opt-in by default and scoped behind a feature toggle (enable_polyglot_adapter) and two request-level headers: X-Redwood-API-Schema (values: v1, v2, v3) and X-Redwood-Enable-Polyglot (true|false). It also respects Prefer-Schema-Version for explicit negotiation. Key behaviours: - For streaming endpoints, the adapter rewrites event frames from older formats into the new v3 delta/frame shape and preserves final structured payloads for tool/function calls. It includes a lightweight mapping layer for legacy "tool_call" fields and fallback to plain text when an unknown tool schema is encountered. - For function/tool calling, the adapter maps legacy function invocation envelopes to the runtime's structured tool invocation format, converting parameter serialization from form-encoded/opaque strings into JSON object parameters when possible; when conversion is lossy a warning field is injected into the response metadata. - Structured output: legacy "response_format" flags (e.g., text, json_string) are mapped to the v3 structured_output schema; the adapter can synthesize minimal schema wrappers to keep caller code working. - Deprecation mode: when schema v1/v2 is observed and the tenant is not opted into long-term compatibility, the adapter injects a deprecation header (X-Redwood-Schema-Deprecation: “will-disable-2025-02-01”) and increments a usage metric. - Observability: new counters and histograms (polyglot.request_count, polyglot.translation_latency, polyglot.fallback_rate) plus per-request debug hooks when X-Redwood-Debug is present. Implementation highlights: - New package redwood-openai-compat/adapter/polyglot_adapter.go: negotiation logic, header parsing, feature-flag gating. - Streaming bridge: gateway/streaming/polyglot_stream_bridge.go with frame-by-frame re-emission and small buffering to ensure stable backpressure. - Tool-call translation: runtime/tool_adapter/translator.go with canonical map of legacy->v3 parameter shapes and loss/warning metadata. - Test coverage: unit tests for negotiation and translation, integration e2e test that runs a simulated v1 client through the hosted routing layer, and a perf microbenchmark to measure translation overhead. Migration + rollout plan: - Phase 0 (launch): feature off by default; enable for specific tenants via console toggle and support request. - Phase 1 (opt-in beta): allow global header X-Redwood-Enable-Polyglot=true for short-term testing; collect metrics and surfacing in console. - Phase 2 (deprecation warning): if adoption plateaus, send deprecation headers to remaining traffic and open migration guides. - Final: scheduled decommission window communicated 90 days before removal. Backwards/incompatibility notes: the adapter attempts lossless conversion where possible but will fall back to text-only responses when legacy messages include arbitrary binary/opaque payloads. This PR intentionally avoids making the adapter default; turning it on for all traffic is a separate rollout once migration tooling is mature. Security review: parameter translation sanitizes function call arguments and preserves original payloads in request audit logs only when tenant config allows. The adapter delegates auth checks to existing gateway logic; no new authentication surface has been added. Performance: microbenchmarks show median translation latency ~0.9ms per request, p99 ~8.4ms under synthetic load. Streaming frames add negligible latency when no conversion is necessary. Metrics and dashboards added to console for monitoring. Docs and examples: - docs/openai-compat/migration/polyglot-adapter.md added with header usage examples and table mapping common legacy flags to v3 shapes. - example clients in redwood-openai-compat/examples/v1-client-simulate demonstrate graceful upgrade paths. Rollback: feature flag off and automatic passthrough to existing compatibility proxy (fallback) available; CI gating ensures we can disable adapter quickly.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Nice end-to-end. A few concerns: can we avoid buffering entire streaming messages for translation? Please ensure we handle backpressure carefully.
Maya Chen (author): Updated streaming bridge to do frame-by-frame minimal buffering and added tests simulating slow consumers. Also exposed buffering_limit in config.
Liam O'Connor: Add metric for 'translation_lossy' so we can track when conversions drop to text-only.
Maya Chen: Added polyglot.translation_lossy counter and a warning metadata field in response envelope. Also added an integration test asserting the counter increments.
Sofia Diaz: Security review: ensure serialized parameters are sanitized before writing to audit logs. Also confirm KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments.
Maya Chen: Sanitization added; audit log emission gated by tenant.audit_logs.enabled and uses masking for sensitive fields. Documented in migration guide.
